catalog_quote: Based on the above definitions, Naayì is a tone language. This is because, the tone of Naayì has both lexical and grammatical functions as illustrated in (§ 2.7.3). As for the typology of a stress language versus a tone language Yip, 2002 4, Naayì is not a stress language as far as any tone-bearing unit (or every syllable) can bear any tone (free tone). The lexical items associated with tonal melodies are also chosen from an unrestricted set of words in Naayì. This means that a set of words in the same word class that have the same syllable structure can be divided into different groups just by their tone melodies' patterns. Hence, Naayì is not stress or accent language; rather it is tonal language. Therefore, this point strengthens Aklilu s 1990 443 work in which it is recognized that Naayì is tonal. ... Naayì has three level tonemes high H, mid M and low L . These three tonemes are …

new_statements.relation_note: The catalog record for Naayì carries an empty rule and no existing stress statements. This source refines the empty record by establishing the prosodic type: three contrastive tones, no stress described. The report points to 'Aklilu 1991' for 'a detailed description of the Nayi phonology' (p. 6), which is not among the listed works; the bibliography (p. 31) lists an undated 'Two phonological processes in Nayi: palatalization and labialization' in Taddese et al. eds 1990, which would be the place to look for any stress remark. The open_url (sil.org abstract.asp) returned a not reachable by automated download
new_statements.rule_in_words: Nayi is described as a three-tone language (High, Mid unmarked, Low); tone is lexical and grammatical (it alone distinguishes 1sg vs 1pl possessive affixes). The report has no stress or accent section and never uses the words stress, accent or prominence (a full-text search for stress/accent found nothing in 31 pp.), so it makes no statement about word stress at all.
new_statements.identity_note: Aklilu Yilma 2002 covers Nayi (Na'o) of the Decha Awraja villages Goba, Gushi, Angela-Menesh and Udadish (Kefa region, near Bonga), with migrant settlements near Bonga, in Dulkuma (Shoa Bench Wereda) and in Aybera, Kosa and Jomdos (Sheko Wereda); it does not distinguish dialects in the phonology section. Language name in the report: Nayi (Na'o); ISO noz; Glottolog nayi1243.
